grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Simple Present Wh-Questions
grammarPoints.rule: Use 'What does [subject] do?' to ask about someone's job. Use 'Where does [subject] work?' to ask about their workplace. Respond with '[Subject] is a [job]' or '[Subject] works in/on/at [place]' using the third-person singular form of verbs.
grammarPoints.pattern: What does... do? / Where does... work?

rules.title: Use 'does' for singular subjects in questions
rules.jp_title: 三人称単数の疑問文には 'does' を使う
rules.subtitle: Always use 'does' (not 'do') when asking questions about a singular person like father, mother, or she/he.
rules.jp_subtitle: お父さん、お母さん、彼・彼女など、一人の人について質問するときは、'do' ではなく常に 'does' を使います。

examples.jp: あなたの姉（妹）は何をしていますか？

rules.title: Use base verb form in questions with 'does'
rules.jp_title: doesの後ろの動詞は原形にする
rules.subtitle: In a question with 'does', the main verb (do or work) must be in its base form. Do not add 's' to the verb in the question.
rules.jp_subtitle: 'does' を使った疑問文では、メインの動詞（do または work）は原形（sのない形）にする必要があります。

examples.jp: 彼はどこで働いていますか？

rules.title: Add '-s' or '-es' to action verbs in answers
rules.jp_title: 主語が三人称単数の肯定文では動詞に 's/es' をつける
rules.subtitle: In answers, use third-person singular verbs like 'works', 'teaches', 'goes', or 'drives' when talking about he, she, or one person.
rules.jp_subtitle: 答えの中で、彼や彼女、あるいは一人の人について話すときは、'works' や 'teaches' のような三人称単数形の動詞を使います。

rules.title: Using correct prepositions for workplaces
rules.jp_title: 職場に合わせた正しい前置詞（in/on/at）を使う
rules.subtitle: Use 'in' for buildings (office, hospital, bank, kitchen), 'on' for surfaces/vehicles (farm, train), and 'at' for home.
rules.jp_subtitle: 建物（オフィス、病院、銀行、キッチン）には 'in'、平面や乗り物（農場、列車）には 'on'、自宅には 'at' を使います。

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Want + Infinitive
grammarPoints.shortName: want to be for future jobs
grammarPoints.rule: Use 'What do you want to be?' to ask about someone's future job or dream. Respond with 'I want to be a/an [job].' Use 'What does he/she want to be?' and respond with 'He/She wants to be a/an [job].' Use 'What do they want to be?' and respond with 'They want to be [jobs].'
grammarPoints.pattern: What do/does + [subject] + want to be? / [Subject] + want/wants to be + a/an + [job]

intro_examples.text: What do you want to be? I want to be a movie star.
intro_examples.jp: あなたは何になりたいですか？私は映画スターになりたいです。

intro_examples.text: What does your brother want to be? He wants to be a doctor.
intro_examples.jp: あなたのお兄さんは何になりたいですか？彼は医師（お医者さん）になりたいです。

table.title: Asking and Answering about Dream Jobs

cells: What do + I/you/we/they + want to be?
What do you want to be?
I want to be a movie star.
What does + he/she/singular + want to be?
What does your brother want to be?
He wants to be a doctor.

notes: In questions, always use the base form 'want' (not 'wants') with 'do' or 'does'.
In singular answers, add 's' to make 'wants to be a/an [job]'.
Use 'an' before vowel sounds (an artist, an inventor, an office worker) and 'a' before consonant sounds (a chef, a vet, a rock star).

japanese.title: want + 不定詞（〜になりたい）
japanese.rule: 「What do you want to be?」（あなたは何になりたいですか？）や主語が三人称単数の場合は「What does he/she want to be?」（彼・彼女は何になりたいですか？）を使い、夢の職業について尋ねます。答え方は「I want to be a/an [職業]」または「He/She wants to be a/an [職業]」のように答えます。
japanese.pattern: What do/does... want to be? / ... want/wants to be...
